title: 1991 Indian economic liberalisation
summary: In July 1991, after a foreign-exchange crisis, India devalued the rupee in two steps and cut import restrictions. On 24 July a new industrial policy removed about 80% of industry from the License Raj, and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh presented a budget opening the economy.

as_recorded.value: on 24 July 1991, the then finance minister Manmohan Singh had unveiled the historic budget
July 1: two-stage devaluation of the rupee; July 24: new industrial policy removes about 80% of Indian industry from the License Raj

where.modern_name: India (national policy; pin is a country-level reference point)

importance.justification: Sources describe the budget as a break from socialism that opened the economy to foreign investment.
